config_name: Gigabyte Gaming A16 — Core i7-13620H / RTX 5060, 24GB RAM, 1TB SSD

specs.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop 8GB GDDR7 (~85W TGP)
specs.ports: 1x USB-C (PD, no Thunderbolt/USB4), 2x USB-A 3.0, 1x USB 2.0, HDMI, gigabit Ethernet, 3.5mm

battery.notes: 76Wh; ~6-7h light use per NBC platform verdict.

price.notes: BBY API-verified 2026-11-24. Two near-identical tiers consolidated: SKU 20341968 (24GB/1TB, reg $2,919.53, sale $2,119.53) and SKU 20340892 (32GB/2TB, reg $3,506.14, sale $2,706.14). Both marketplace sellers — fulfillment/return risk. A sibling 32GB/2TB tier of this SKU sold for ~$2,706 CAD.

reviews.quote: The Gaming A16 earned a good overall score of 80%. On the positive side, the consistent CPU and GPU performance are worth pointing out.

praises: Best price-per-gaming-frame of the lineup at full price: RTX 5060 for ~$2,120 on sale
Consistent sustained performance, good sound, decent battery for class (NBC pros)
32GB/2TB variant covers heavy multitasking without opening the case
complaints: WUXGA 1200p panel is a downgrade vs the NBC-tested WQXGA on the 5070 tier
Very loud fan under load (NBC platform con)
Marketplace listings with inflated 'regular' price anchors — sale price is the real price

design_philosophy: The RTX 5060 tiers are the volume sellers of Gigabyte's value-first Gaming A16 line: same chassis, same upgradeable interior, GPU tier chosen for mainstream 1080p/1200p gaming. Consolidated here because the two BBY tiers differ only in RAM/storage (24GB/1TB and 32GB/2TB).
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from NBC's Gaming A16 GA6H review (80%, i7-13620H/RTX 5070/WQXGA): RTX 5060 vs 5070 -> gaming -1.0, creative_work -0.5; WUXGA panel per retailer -> screen_quality -1.0. 32GB/2TB twin (SKU 20340892) would add +0.5 productivity/ai_ml. BBY per-SKU reviews unavailable — sentiment review-grounded synthesis.
standouts: Best price-per-frame of the Gaming A16 tiers ($2,119 sale for RTX 5060)
dealbreakers: WUXGA panel on this tier (per retailer) vs WQXGA on the reviewed 5070 tier
